A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STAR research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and rendered figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation and inpainting results, order and traversal ablations, and token-entropy analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original STAR experiments and adds inpainting comparisons, center-bias analyses, and CIFAR-100 representation-learning results.

M1.justification: The core architecture and spanning-tree training procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 extends completion to separate trees for disconnected mask components and revises root selection across their boundaries. Appendix A additionally demonstrates successive postfix completions for masks violating the single-pass assumptions.

E1.justification: v2 adds CIFAR-100 representation learning and linear-probe classification, extending coverage beyond ImageNet generation and inpainting. Appendix A also demonstrates an inpainting scenario with all corners masked and disconnected partial observations.

E2.justification: The inpainting comparison expands from RAR to include DiT-XL/2 and RandAR-L/XL in v2 Table 2 and Figure 6. This adds diffusion and flexible-order AR comparators to the central downstream evaluation, although these methods already appeared in the unchanged generation comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include center-bias quartiles evaluated using 50k generated images, and iGPT-S configurations trained on CIFAR-100 for 100k steps with intermediate-feature linear probes and checkpoint perplexity. DiT inpainting uses latent blending. The printed mask sampler additionally excludes masks covering all corners; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of performance across center-bias strengths, extends spatial entropy analysis to STAR, reports sampling overhead, and analyzes representation-learning convergence and overfitting. Appendix A adds a case study outside the single-pass masking assumptions. The earlier order/traversal ablations and appendix sequence-entropy analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 changes the reported entropy-estimation budget from 100 sampled permutations per validation image to 30 sampled orders per image for each analyzed model. This changes the estimator's sampling budget, without establishing additional independent training runs. Neither version reports training-seed counts or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results: Table 2 reports average inpainting FID of 2.07 for STAR-XL, 2.58 for RandAR-XL, 3.40 for RAR-XL, and 4.58 for DiT-XL/2. Figures 8a and 9 add center-bias and representation-learning findings. Table 1 and the retained order/traversal ablation scores are unchanged; the additions are not demonstrated improvements over v1 STAR scores.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 generalizes the boundary-depth argument to multiple disconnected mask components and changes the stated necessary depth inequality from strict greater-than in v1 Equation 3 to greater-than-or-equal in v2 Equation 5. v2 also adds entropy-chain reasoning about ideal order invariance and finite-budget convergence.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: structured spanning-tree orders preserve generation performance, enable flexible inpainting, and require minimal architectural changes. The additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations involving convergence speed, locality, center-bias dependence, and inpainting behavior across model families. Appendix A explicitly discusses realistic violations of masking assumptions, distinguishes single-pass limitations from successive completion, and identifies unexplored traversal and tie-breaking choices.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly identifies the cloud instance and reports 65, 80, 160, and 385 A100 GPU-days across STAR configurations; existing hyperparameters and code access remain unchanged. The rewritten masking pseudocode moves initialization outside the retry loop, leaving resampling after rejection unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Blended Latent Diffusion, DetailFlow, FlowAR, CART, and work connecting permutation AR with masked-model objectives. These additions broaden supporting context while retaining STAR's positioning as a simple structured-order alternative within autoregressive visual generation.

P1.justification: Method motivation and experimental interpretation receive extensive rewriting and reorganization. v2 introduces a Discussion section, reorganizes analyses around locality, center bias, entropy, and overhead, moves the earlier appendix entropy discussion into the main text, and restructures the supplement.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Entropy figures are combined and expanded, the traversal table is transposed, the inpainting comparison panel is rebuilt, and new algorithm, center-bias, representation-learning, and successive-completion illustrations appear. The appendix sample grids are retained.

improvement.justification: The added RandAR and DiT inpainting comparisons address an important evidential gap in v1's central editing claim. Center-bias tests directly examine the design premise, while explicit masking limitations clarify applicability. These gains substantially strengthen the paper despite unchanged headline generation scores and the localized retry-pseudocode omission in Appendix B.
